Both arms achieved optimal ovarian function suppression, with degarelix showing superior speed (3 days vs 14 days for triptorelin). This represents a clinically meaningful improvement in time to therapeutic effect. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analyses were reported, but both treatments worked in the enrolled population of invasive breast cancer patients receiving neoadjuvant therapy. 5. CONFOUNDERS: No major trial design issues. Adequate dosing was achieved, no safety signals reported, and the endpoint directly measured the intended biological effect.
